cloud.notes: The v4.2.1 app's only steady-state device channel is Aqara's cloud: authenticated HTTPS REST "resource write" ({subjectId, dataKey, value}) for control and cloud push for events. Onboarding is also cloud-bound: GET/POST /app/v1.0/lumi/... endpoints issue the bindKey (per positionId/connectType), register BLE devices (dev/bluetooth/reg/*) and generate Matter fabric material (user/cert/matter/home/gen-cac|gen-noc). If the vendor cloud dies: already-provisioned hubs keep their LAN presence (mDNS/whois still answer) but no documented local control path exists in this app generation; adopting a reset hub without the cloud is blocked on the bindKey unless hardware testing shows hubs accept an arbitrary one.

discover_whois.description: Multicast discovery probe: plaintext JSON to 230.0.0.1:10008; hubs answer with iam (see protocol_details.aqara_lan_protocol.multicast_discovery).

provision_wifi.description: Wi-Fi onboarding: AES-128-CBC-encrypted JSON provisioning datagram to the hub on UDP 10008 (or its mDNS-advertised port). Format and crypto in protocol_details.aqara_lan_protocol. Requires a cloud-issued bindKey embedded in the payload.

returns.description: Encrypted JSON; error keys iotError/errorMessage; close with encrypted {"ack":1}
returns.name: provision_result

methods.notes: Service type confirmed from the app's mDNS browser code. TXT: md=model, id=did, pv=true ⇒ already provisioned (a hub in pairing mode advertises without pv or with pv unset). The SRV port is the device's provisioning port; the app defaults to 10008 when absent.

Multicast (not subnet-broadcast) discovery: send plaintext JSON {"command":"whois","address":"<your LAN IP>","port":"<your UDP listen port>"} to group 230.0.0.1 port 10008. Answering devices reply to the given address with a plaintext JSON ARRAY of {"command":"iam","address":"<deviceIP>:<port>","model":"…", "name":"…","registered":"yes|no"}. Whether the probe itself may also go through the app's AES layer is unverifiable from the recovered code (one method body did not survive unpacking); the reply is parsed as plaintext JSON.

identification.notes: On the LAN a hub (or any unprovisioned Aqara Wi-Fi device) advertises `_aqara._tcp` with TXT keys md (model string, e.g. the lumi.* model id), id (device id / did) and pv (`pv=true` means "already provisioned" — the app's own setup list filters those OUT, so for discovery of adoptable units watch for the opposite). The mDNS instance name is the device id. In setup mode the hub hosts a Wi-Fi AP whose SSID matches `lumi-<type>-<suffix>` (observed tokens: gateway, and model-family suffixes like m1s / acn02 / aqhm) or `Aqara Hub *`; the hub answers at 192.x.y.1 (the /24 gateway of whatever address it hands the phone) on UDP 10008.

device.name: Aqara Hub family (M1S Gen 2, M2, AC Partner P3)
device.notes:
Aqara's Wi-Fi hubs bridge the vendor's Zigbee/BLE sensors to Wi-Fi and the cloud; some models add IR blaster (AC Partner P3, M2) or a speaker/ RGB light (M1S). Aqara (Lumi United) is an ACTIVE company — this spec's purpose is documenting the local surface, which turns out to be narrow in the current generation:
WHAT IS LOCAL: hub discovery and Wi-Fi onboarding. An unprovisioned hub answers mDNS `_aqara._tcp.local.` and a UDP multicast "whois" probe to 230.0.0.1:10008, and it takes Wi-Fi credentials over UDP 10008 as AES-128-CBC-encrypted JSON (parameters fully recovered — see aqara_lan_protocol.crypto). Some models accept the same credentials over TCP 10000 plaintext JSON, an HTTPS POST while hosting their setup AP, or BLE "Magic Pair" commissioning.
WHAT IS NOT LOCAL: steady-state control. The v4.2.1 app contains NO post-setup LAN command channel for hubs — no get/read/write verbs, no local event stream, no LAN heartbeat. Arm/disarm, light control, sub-device state, IR blasting and event delivery are all relayed through Aqara's cloud (authenticated REST "resource write" with subjectId/dataKey/value, plus cloud push). The older Xiaomi-era developer-mode LAN protocol (multicast 224.0.0.50, ports 54321/9898, per-hub AES key shown in the app) has NO trace in this app version — third-party projects that still use it (e.g. the Home Assistant AqaraGateway custom integration) depend on enabling developer options on older hub firmware, outside what this document verifies.
CLOUD DEPENDENCY: onboarding is cloud-assisted even though the transport is local — the app fetches a `bindKey` (and region/position IDs) from Aqara's REST API and embeds it in the provisioning payload; account binding completes via cloud polling. The hub's persistent control session is hub→cloud.
RELATED SURFACES (recovered in the same analysis, documented under protocol_details): the Aqara BLE lock family (lumi.lock.*) has a fully mapped local GATT control channel (ECDH P-256 + AES-CCM session) whose binding step is cloud-assisted; Matter commissioning is standard CHIP (BLE 0xFFF6 / _matterc._udp) but fabric certificates are cloud-issued and steady-state Matter control is cloud-relayed in this app version.

openness.notes: Aqara publishes no LAN API for the current hub generation. This spec is recovered from the vendor app's recovered code (see file header). The only documented local interface Aqara ever shipped was the legacy developer-mode protocol on older firmware, which this app version no longer speaks.

credentials.notes: The Wi-Fi passphrase travels AES-128-CBC encrypted with an app-wide key (recovered, aqara_lan_protocol.crypto) — over-the-air protection only; the key is public once the app is analyzed, so treat the setup-AP window as the sensitive moment. The bindKey is bound to the account/position and is not a reusable client credential.

factory_reset.effect: Two reset scopes (vendor-documented): holding the button ~10 s until the yellow LED flashes resets the NETWORK connection only (Zigbee child bindings survive — this is the router-replacement move); pressing the button 10 times (M1S Gen 2, per its manual) restores factory defaults including bindings. Either way the hub must be re-onboarded afterwards, which requires the vendor cloud (bindKey).

procedures.basis: Vendor help center (Aqara Hub M2) and M1S Gen 2 manual: hold ~10 s until the yellow LED flashes.
procedures.name: Network reset (button hold)

steps.action: With the hub powered, hold its button for about 10 seconds.
steps.expect: Yellow/red LED flashes quickly; hub forgets Wi-Fi and re-enters pairing.

procedures.basis: M1S Gen 2 vendor manual (button press table): 10 presses restore factory defaults.
procedures.name: Full factory reset (M1S Gen 2: button ×10)

steps.action: Press the hub button 10 times in succession.
steps.expect: Hub restores factory defaults; child-device bindings are cleared.

methods.description: The phone joins the hub's temporary AP, derives the hub address as 192.x.y.1, and sends the Wi-Fi credentials as AES-128-CBC encrypted JSON in one UDP datagram to port 10008. The hub replies (encrypted), and the app closes with an encrypted {"ack":1}. The full payload format and crypto are in aqara_lan_protocol.
methods.name: Setup-AP + encrypted UDP credential push (port 10008)

provisioning_request.description: JSON {"cid":" ","ssid":"<home ssid>","passwd":"<wifi password>", "lang":"<locale>","bindKey":"<cloud-issued>", "country_domain":"<region>","timeZone":"GMT±h[:mm]"} — optional extra keys positionId, uid, baseUrl — then AES-128-CBC encrypted (aqara_lan_protocol.crypto) and sent as a single datagram.

provisioning_response.description: Encrypted JSON; the app checks keys iotError / errorMessage. On success the app sends encrypted {"ack":1}.

softap.gateway_ip: 192.x.y.1 (the /24 gateway of the address the hub's DHCP hands the phone)

steps.action: Reset the hub (or it ships fresh) so it hosts its setup AP.
steps.expect: An SSID matching lumi-gateway-* / 'Aqara Hub *' appears.

steps.action: Join that AP from the client machine.
steps.expect: Client gets a 192.x.y.z lease; hub is 192.x.y.1.

steps.action: Send the encrypted provisioning JSON to 192.x.y.1:10008 (format in aqara_lan_protocol).
steps.expect: Encrypted reply without iotError; hub joins the home Wi-Fi and starts answering _aqara._tcp on the LAN.

causes: The bindKey inside the payload is issued by Aqara's cloud REST API for the target positionId; whether a hub accepts an arbitrary bindKey offline has not been tested (no hardware).
Wrong band: the hubs are 802.11b/g/n 2.4 GHz only.
troubleshooting.symptom: Hub never completes onboarding even though the UDP exchange answers.

methods.description: Some models take credentials as an HTTPS POST while hosting the setup AP: JSON {"wifi":"<ssid>","pwd":"<password>","cid":" ", "bindKey":"…","country_domain":"…"} followed by a second POST {"ack":1}. The app's built-in default URL reads https://192.168.5.1:4567/<path>, but the path in the binary is a placeholder and the real endpoint is pushed per-device from server config — treat the exact URL as UNVERIFIED until captured from a real hub.
methods.name: Setup-AP + HTTPS POST (ap_http models)

steps.action: Join the hub's setup AP, then POST the credential JSON to its HTTPS endpoint.
steps.expect: HTTP 200, then a second POST {"ack":1} completes the handoff.

methods.description: Newer hubs (and other Aqara Wi-Fi devices) advertise a BLE commissioning surface: GATT service 0000fcb9-0000-1000-8000- 00805f9b34fb (write 0000ff07-…, notify 0000ff08-…) carrying a Weave-style TLV provisioning dialogue, with a TLV advertisement (vendor id / product id / discriminator / commissioned flag). Matter-capable models expose standard CHIP commissioning instead (BLE service 0xFFF6, or _matterc._udp for on-network commissioning). Both flows hand over Wi-Fi credentials locally but complete binding against Aqara's cloud (Matter fabric certificates are generated by Aqara REST endpoints).
methods.name: BLE Magic Pair commissioning

steps.action: Scan BLE for the hub's commissioning advertisement while it is in pairing mode.

methods.description: Hubs with an RJ45 port (M2) skip the setup AP entirely: plug in Ethernet, find the hub with the multicast whois probe (discovery block) or mDNS, and push the same encrypted provisioning JSON to its LAN address on UDP 10008.
methods.name: Ethernet models: multicast whois + UDP 10008

steps.action: Connect the hub to the router over Ethernet and power it.
steps.expect: Hub answers whois multicast and _aqara._tcp on the LAN.

setup.notes: A factory/reset hub cannot be used until it joins Wi-Fi AND is bound to an Aqara account: the Wi-Fi credential handoff is fully local (encrypted UDP below), but the payload embeds a cloud-issued bindKey and the app confirms onboarding by polling the cloud. Aqara's cloud being alive is therefore a hard requirement for adopting a reset hub as designed — a key fact for this registry's purpose. The app selects among several per-model delivery modes (its own words: ap_udp, ap_tcp, ap_http, ethernet, ble_gateway, magic_pair, matter, …); the methods below are ordered by how reproducible they are from this document.

rejoin.notes: The 10-second network reset re-points the hub at a new Wi-Fi network without wiping Zigbee children (per vendor help center and user reports); full ×10 factory reset is the clean-slate fallback.

testing.notes: No Aqara hub is in the project's test hardware pool, so no packet here has been replayed against real hardware. Everything comes from static analysis of the recovered Aqara Home 4.2.1 app code. ONE part is hardware-verified: the provisioning datagram crypto (AES-128-CBC parameters in aqara_lan_protocol.crypto) was confirmed against the vendor's own crypto library running on a rooted Android device — known plaintexts encrypt to the library's exact outputs. The discovery whois/iam exchange, the provisioning JSON keys and the port numbers are read from code, not sniffed from a live hub.

variants.notes: Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz + Zigbee 3.0 hub with RGB night light and 2 W speaker; button: single press toggles the light, 10 s hold resets network, ×10 press factory-resets (vendor manual).
Adds Ethernet (RJ45) and an IR blaster; vendor help center documents the 10 s hold reset. The app's IR remote surface for this family is cloud-relayed (no local IR protocol in the app).

covers: LAN discovery and identification of hubs (mDNS + multicast whois)
Wi-Fi credential delivery (encrypted UDP 10008, TCP 10000, setup-AP HTTPS variants)
not_covered: Any steady-state control: arm/disarm, hub light/speaker, IR blaster
Adopting a reset hub without the vendor cloud (bindKey)
local_access.summary: For CONTROL, no local path exists in the current app/firmware generation — an honest dead end as shipped: the app drives hubs and their Zigbee children exclusively through the vendor cloud. Locally you CAN discover hubs (mDNS _aqara._tcp / multicast whois) and perform the Wi-Fi onboarding transport (AES-128-CBC encrypted UDP 10008, parameters recovered). For the pre-2022 hub generation a developer-mode LAN control protocol was documented by third parties (see helpful_urls), but it is absent from the current app and unverified here.

ble_lock_family.framing: 2-byte command header (mainCmd, subCmd); mainCmd 0x01 system / 0x02 user / 0x03 record / 0x04 alarm / 0x3F long / 0x81 reply / 0xBF long-reply; fragmented writes, final fragment id 0xFF; registration frames CRC16-protected
ble_lock_family.security: ECDH secp256r1 key exchange → AES-CCM session (13-byte nonce); 25 s application heartbeat

services.data: 0000ff60-2333-5b1e-9d7c-c687fd2f04f2 (write ff61, notify ff62, OTA write ff63, OTA notify ff64, same base)
services.magic_pair: 0000fcb9-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (write ff07, notify ff08) — gateway commissioning, not locks

ble_lock_family.summary: Aqara's BLE locks (lumi.lock.acn02/03/04/06, aq1, dq1, n100, s2, s2pro, net) speak a local GATT protocol recovered in the same analysis. Control after binding is fully local; binding/log-in is cloud-assisted (ECDH publickey exchange + assure endpoints). Worth a dedicated spec when hardware is available.

crypto.algorithm: AES-128-CBC, PKCS7 padding, no per-message IV on the wire
crypto.determinism: no random IV — same plaintext always yields the same ciphertext
crypto.scope: app-wide constants from the bundled native crypto library; used for the UDP provisioning datagrams and their replies
crypto.verification: Verified 2026-08-29 against the vendor library itself (driven on-device): with key "Uw4i98shjoeUQdaD" and the IV above, AES-128-CBC/PKCS7 of "" is caca794f590e57df25730a7462fc7644, of "A" is c7ecb89c15608887cf9dd16e9ac6b038, of "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA" is 6cac6e23b9fcd71f166859a4d028c8e42fe0b189b4da6a0baf2eb935afacc2e2, and of 64 "A" bytes is 6cac6e23…(first block repeated scheme)… — all four byte-for-byte identical to the library's output.

matter.summary: Matter-capable models commission via stock CHIP: BLE service 0000FFF6-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB or NSD _matterc._udp.local., PASE with the printed/manual pincode, then NetworkCredentials (Wi-Fi or Thread). Fabric certificates and node IDs are generated by Aqara's cloud (REST gen-cac/gen-noc/gen-nodeid) and steady-state control is cloud-relayed in this app version.

txt_keys.pv: 'true' when already provisioned; absent/unset in pairing mode

multicast_discovery.reply: Plaintext JSON array, one object per answering device: [{"command":"iam","address":"<deviceIP>:<port>","model":"…", "name":"…","registered":"yes|no"}]

provisioning_https_ap.endpoint_default: https://192.168.5.1:4567/<path> — path is a placeholder in the binary; real value is server-pushed per device model. UNVERIFIED.

provisioning_tcp.encryption: none visible in the recovered code

provisioning_udp.ack: {"ack":1} — encrypted, sent after a successful reply
provisioning_udp.direction: client → hub, one datagram; hub replies; client closes with ack
provisioning_udp.reply: encrypted JSON; error keys iotError / errorMessage
provisioning_udp.socket_behavior: receive timeout ~5 s, receive buffer 102400 bytes (app side)

remaining_unknowns: Whether a hub accepts an arbitrary bindKey in the provisioning payload when the vendor cloud is unreachable (needs hardware; decides whether offline adoption of reset hubs is possible).
The HTTPS setup-AP endpoint path and whether 192.168.5.1:4567 is the real default (placeholder-looking value in the binary; server-pushed per model).
Whether the whois multicast probe is additionally wrapped in the AES layer on some firmware (one code path did not survive unpacking).
BLE lock sub-command byte values and the advertisement bit packing (hidden behind the packer's JNI indirection in the dump).
Legacy developer-mode LAN control protocol on older hub firmware: documented by third parties (Home Assistant AqaraGateway), absent from the current app — not verified by this project.
